summary: EMA Trend Gate strategy on BTCUSDT 1h (43,789 bars, ~5 years) achieved 0.998 OOS Sharpe with 848 trades across 57 windows, validating the hypothesis that BTC's higher volatility generates better risk-adjusted returns than ETH baseline (0.528 Sharpe, -16.37% DD). Key improvements: +89% Sharpe, +58% drawdown reduction.

key_lessons.lesson: Cross-asset generalization validated: BTC outperforms ETH baseline
key_lessons.specific_finding: BTC achieved 0.998 OOS Sharpe vs ETH 0.528 (+89% improvement), with significantly better drawdown profile (-6.9% vs -16.37%, +58% improvement)
14.88 trades/window on BTC vs 14.3 on ETH (+4%), confirming strategy generates consistent opportunities on higher-volatility assets
RSI thresholds stable (CV=0.10-0.14) across 57 windows, but hold_bars unstable (CV=0.43) - same pattern as ETH run (CV=0.54)

key_lessons.lesson: WFR remains uncomputed due to engine limitation
key_lessons.specific_finding: WFA engine does not output IS Sharpe, preventing WFR calculation - this affects all factory experiments, not specific to this run

next_actions.action: Pin hold_bars to median range (48-72 bars) and re-optimize to reduce parameter instability
next_actions.rationale: hold_bars shows CV=0.43 (unstable) on both ETH and BTC runs; pinning to stable range may improve robustness without sacrificing performance

next_actions.action: Test on other major crypto pairs (BNB, SOL) to further validate cross-asset generalization
next_actions.rationale: BTC shows strong generalization vs ETH; testing on additional assets will strengthen evidence base for strategy family

next_actions.action: Consider extending to larger timeframe combination (4h/1h already tested, try 8h/4h)
next_actions.rationale: Strategy leverages 4h regime filter + 1h entry; larger timeframes may capture broader trends with similar pullback logic
